# Keep tooltips within screen bounds

## Problem statement

Tooltips are rendered at a fixed offset from the hover point without any viewport-bounds checking. When a hovered element sits near the right or bottom edge of the window, the tooltip overflows the viewport; in the DOM-rendered mode this extends the document's scrollable area, so the page "resizes to make space" (scrollbars appear / layout shifts). The tooltip must always be positioned so that it is fully visible and never alters the document layout.

## Users

- **Players** hovering cards, HUD elements, and buttons in Main Street, Lost Cities, Sushi Go, and the Gym tooltip/Gym-card-index demos.
- **Engine consumers (game developers)** who rely on the shared `TooltipManager` (DOM and Phaser modes) so they do not have to re-implement bounds handling per game.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I hover a card near the right edge of the screen, the tooltip appears fully on-screen instead of being clipped or pushing the page wider.
- As a player, showing a tooltip never causes the game canvas or page to jump/resize.
- As a game developer, when I supply a `phaserRender` callback I can clamp my tooltip into the game canvas with a shared helper rather than copying clamp maths between games.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DOM-mode clamping:** For a hover point near each of the four viewport edges, the DOM tooltip's rendered bounding rectangle is fully inside the browser viewport (`left >= 0`, `top >= 0`, `right <= window.innerWidth`, `bottom <= window.innerHeight`), with a small margin. Verified by a browser (`*.browser.test.ts`) test in `tests/ui/`.
2. **No document resize:** Showing (and hiding) a DOM tooltip does not change the document scroll size — no horizontal/vertical scrollbar is introduced (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` before and after `show()`). Verified by a browser test.
3. **Phaser-mode clamping:** The shared Phaser render callbacks keep their tooltip containers inside the game canvas bounds (`0..GAME_W` × `0..GAME_H`) at all four edges. Gym's callback (currently unclamped) is brought in line with the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, ideally via a shared, unit-tested helper. Verified by unit tests (helper) plus the existing scene/browser tests.
4. **No regression to existing positioning:** Existing world→screen coordinate mapping (canvas scale, canvas offset, camera scroll) and the settings `showTooltips` toggle behaviour are preserved; the existing `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` / `TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` expectations are updated rather than weakened.
5. **Validation and documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (tooltip component section) and any relevant Gym help text. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Must not regress reduced-motion, `pointer-events: none`, or the maximum `z-index` behaviour of the DOM tooltip.
- Must remain safe in non-DOM environments (`document`/`window` undefined) and when the canvas bounding rect cannot be read — fall back to hiding, as today.
- Clamping must be cheap (measure once per `show()`, no per-frame layout thrash, no resize listeners).
- The DOM tooltip node must not contribute to the document's scrollable overflow area.
- Use UK English in comments and docs; escape only backticks in worklog content.
- Existing tests that assert `div.style.position === 'absolute'` will need updating if the positioning strategy changes (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManager`. DOM mode computes `screenX`/`screenY` from the canvas rect, camera scroll, and scale, then sets `left`/`top` = point + `(10, 10)` offset with **no bounds check**. The node is `position: absolute`, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 2147483647`, `max-width: 320px`, appended to `document.body`. Phaser mode delegates layout entirely to the caller's `phaserRender` callback.
- Consumers in DOM mode: Main Street (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` constructs it; `MainStreetRendererStreet/Hud/Market/Layout.ts` call `show`), `GymTooltipScene` DOM half, `GymCardIndexScene`.
- Consumers in Phaser mode: `LostCitiesScene.ts` (`createTooltipManager`) and `SushiGoScene.ts` — both already clamp with `Phaser.Math.Clamp(..., 4, GAME_W - boxW - 4)` etc. `GymTooltipScene`'s Phaser callback does **not** clamp.
- Tests: `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` (unit), `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` (browser, asserts `position === 'absolute'`), `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` (SLL anchors only), plus Main Street tooltip content tests.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents `TooltipManager`; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` maps the tooltip scenes.

## Desired change

- Add viewport-bounds clamping to the shared DOM tooltip renderer in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`:
  - Position the node relative to the viewport so it cannot extend the document scroll area (e.g. `position: fixed`).
  - Measure the node after setting content, then flip it above/left of the hover point when there is not enough room below/right, and clamp to the viewport as a final guard, keeping a small margin.
  - Keep the existing world→screen conversion (canvas rect + camera scroll + scale).
- Extract a reusable bounds-clamping helper for in-canvas (Phaser) tooltips, mirroring the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, and use it in `GymTooltipScene` (and optionally migrate Lost Cities / Sushi Go to the shared helper with no behaviour change).
- Add unit tests for the clamp maths (all four edges, both axes, oversized tooltip) and browser tests proving the tooltip stays in the viewport and does not change document scroll size.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and Gym help text if the scene behaviour/description changes).
- **Test-first:** author the clamp-helper unit tests and the browser edge/document-scroll tests before wiring the DOM renderer and the Gym callback, so the new behaviour is specified by failing tests first.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — Add DOM-mode viewport clamping / anti-resize positioning; export a reusable Phaser-mode clamp helper.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — Apply the clamp helper in the `phaserRender` callback (currently unclamped).
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — Unit tests for clamp maths via the DOM mock and helper.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — Edge-position + document-scroll-size assertions; update the `position` selector assumption.
- `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` — Extend with Gym Phaser-mode in-bounds assertions (if the scene callback is changed).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the bounds guarantee for both tooltip modes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the correct, complete interpretation of the title is "no tooltip (in either DOM or Phaser mode) may render outside its visible bounds", not just the DOM overlay. The DOM mode is the cause of the reported page-resize; Phaser mode only clips. Recommended and assumed.
- **Assumption:** clamping (shift/flip to stay visible) is preferred over truncating content or shrinking the tooltip. Documented assumption; trivially revisitable.
- **Risk:** switching the DOM node to `position: fixed` invalidates the existing browser test's `position === 'absolute'` selector — update the selector to target the tooltip by its stable attributes (`pointer-events: none` + `z-index`) rather than `position`.
- **Risk:** measuring the node to clamp requires it to be laid out; setting `display: block` before measuring may cause a one-frame flash. Mitigate by measuring immediately after content is set and before paint (single synchronous reflow), or measure with `visibility: hidden` then reveal.
- **Risk:** `window`/`document` may be undefined in unit tests/SSR — guard clamping behind the existing `document` checks and fall back to the unclamped path (or hide) when dimensions are unavailable.
- **Risk:** double clamping when a game's `phaserRender` already clamps — the helper must be opt-in and not re-apply automatically to caller-managed containers.
- **Risk:** oversized tooltips (taller/wider than the viewport) cannot fit; clamp to the margin and accept partial visibility, documenting the behaviour.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tooltip content wrapping/truncation, touch/long-press tooltips, and tooltip theming are out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Related work

- **CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7** – Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover (completed) — introduced the shared `TooltipManager` this bug affects.
- **CG-0MODIX70W002JXQN** – `feat(ui): add TooltipManager` / `fix(ui): DOM-positioned tooltip displays above cards` — prior DOM coordinate-mapping work in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`.
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed) — SLL precedent for declarative positioning.
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed) — SLL layout system; relevant if bounds handling is expressed via SLL zones.
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed) — Main Street tooltip content fix, no overlap with positioning.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed)
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ake, bounds, displayed, ensure, keep (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+10 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+7 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q:** Are there open questions requiring producer input? — **A:** No. The seed context ("Sometimes when a tooltip is displayed it would render outside the screen bounds. This results in the screen resizing to make space. We need to ensure that the tooltip is positioned such that it stays within screen bounds.") plus repository research was sufficient to draft a clear, testable brief. No interview round was required. Source: seed context supplied with the intake invocation + repo inspection.

**Prior related answers:** none.

**Research summary:** Inspected `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` (DOM node is `position: absolute` on `document.body` with no bounds check — the resize cause; Phaser mode delegates to `phaserRender`), the four in-repo consumers (Main Street, Gym DOM, Gym Phaser, Lost Cities, Sushi Go), and the existing tests/docs. Lost Cities and Sushi Go already clamp inside the canvas with `Phaser.Math.Clamp`; Gym and the DOM renderer do not. No existing shared clamp helper exists. Related completed tooltip work items were found via `wl search` (see automated report).

# Task: Create the nine `tce-*` GitHub repositories and push extracted history

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer I can clone each per-game repository
(`tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`,
`tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`) plus
`tableau-card-engine-core` from GitHub with `--recurse-submodules`, then run
`npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit`, and get a runnable
single-game TCE checkout — so the sibling-repo composition that F4/F9 built and
verified **locally** exists on the remote and is cloneable by anyone.

## Users (user stories)

- **Distribution maintainer** — creates the nine remotes **once**, in the final
  F9 Option C `src/` layout, so no history-rewriting re-push is ever needed.
- **Game developer** — `git clone --recurse-submodules
  git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-golf.git` and builds/tests the game against
  the engine pulled in as the `core` submodule.
- **Launcher / distribution builder** — composes a subset of the remote game
  repos as siblings (the `solo` and `full` presets) against fresh clones.

## Context

Split out of F4 (CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK) per operator decision: F4 delivers the
local per-game launcher scaffold (configs, `GAME_INFO`, build/test/package,
history-preserving extraction); creating and pushing the remote repositories is
a separate concern. The F4 producer gate deferred remote creation until the F9
Option C `src/` layout settled, so the nine repos are created **once, in the
final `src/` shape** — no history-rewriting re-push.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The nine repositories exist on GitHub under `TheWizardsCode` at the remotes
   recorded in `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`:
   `tableau-card-engine-core`, `tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`,
   `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`,
   `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto`.
2. Each repository's default branch contains the extracted,
   history-preserving tree in the F9 `src/` layout (extraction via
   `scripts/extract-repos.sh`, scaffold via `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`):
   the core repo holds the engine + Gym + launcher shell and **no games**; each
   game repo has its source at repo-root `src/` and wires the engine as a
   `core` git submodule pointing at
   `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`.
3. From a **fresh remote clone**, `git clone --recurse-submodules <game-repo>`
   followed by `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm test -- --project unit`
   succeeds for at least **golf** and **main-street**.
4. The launcher can compose a subset of the **remote** repos as siblings (spot
   check: the `solo` and `full` presets build against fresh clones).
5. Evidence is recorded on this work item: the extraction commit count per repo
   (as F1 did) and the source monorepo commit SHA the nine repos were extracted
   from.
6. No CI pipeline and no npm publication are added (out of scope, per the epic
   constraints).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. (In practice:
   `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 currently says the remotes are
   *not* created; `README.md`/`docs/DEVELOPER.md` clone guidance must document
   the `--recurse-submodules` workflow.)
8. Validation for the change: the extraction/scaffold unit suites
   (`tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts`,
   `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`) pass, and the published remotes
   are validated by the fresh-clone checks in AC3/AC4.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No CI pipeline and no npm publication (epic constraint).
- Never rewrite the source monorepo: extraction always operates on a clone
  (`git clone --no-local`); the monorepo `main` is never pushed to directly.
- `git filter-repo` is required and is **not currently installed** on this host
  (`pip install git-filter-repo` per
  `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`).
- GitHub org write access is required; the authenticated account
  (`SorraTheOrc`) is an **admin** of the `TheWizardsCode` org, so credentials are
  available and creating repos is permitted.
- Remotes use SSH (`git@github.com:...`), consistent with `repo-layout.json`.
- Repos are created once, after F9, in the final `src/` layout.
- **Visibility:** all nine repos are created **public** (producer answer, Q1).
- **Published refs:** push only `dev` plus `main` seeded from it; do **not**
  push the monorepo's feature/`wl-*` branches or its `v0.1.x` tags (Q4).
- **Source revision:** extract from the current `dev` HEAD and record its SHA
  as evidence (producer answer, Q3).

## Existing state

- **F1** delivered `scripts/extract-repos.sh` +
  `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` (history-preserving extraction; verified
  locally: 852 core commits, 23–995 per game).
- **F2** delivered the core-engine repo tree (locally verified standalone).
- **F4** delivered `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` and local per-game checkouts;
  GitHub remote creation was explicitly out of scope (producer gate).
- **F9** reworked per-game repos to repo-root `src/` with alias-only engine
  imports.
- **F5/F7** delivered the launcher distribution and integration verification
  against local sibling checkouts.
- Verified as part of intake: **none** of the nine remotes exist on GitHub
  (`gh api repos/TheWizardsCode/<repo>` → 404).
- The `solo` preset is golf-only; the `full` preset covers all eight games.

## Desired change

Extract all nine repos from the monorepo at the current `dev` HEAD, scaffold the
eight game repos, commit, create the nine GitHub repositories, push each repo's
history to its default branch, and record the per-repo commit counts plus the
source SHA as evidence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/extract-repos.sh` — drives `--target <name>` extraction for the nine
  targets; may need an end-to-end "create remote + push" helper or documented
  commands.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — scaffolds each extracted game checkout.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — source of truth for names/remotes/paths
  (already final; read-only for this task).
- `configs/solo.json`, `configs/full.json` — spot-check sibling composition.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 "GitHub remotes are not created in
  this phase" must be updated to the published state.
- `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — clone-with-submodules instructions.
- `.gitmodules` (per game repo) — `core` submodule wiring.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Visibility / branch model / source revision** — resolved by the producer
  (public; `dev`→`main` with `main` seeded once; current `dev` HEAD with SHA
  recorded); see Appendix Q1–Q3.
- **Published refs** — the filtered clone inherits ~150 branches and 17
  `v0.1.x` tags; publishing only `dev`+`main` avoids stale-branch and cross-repo
  tag confusion (Appendix Q4).
- **History** — preserved as content/provenance, but retained commits receive
  **new SHAs** (inherent to a filtered subset); see Appendix Q3 research.
- `git filter-repo` is not installed on this host — a blocker for real runs
  (fine for `--dry-run`).
- The extraction renames `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` (`--path-rename`) and
  the scaffold rewrites intra-test paths; both history-preserving behaviours were
  verified by F9.
- **Scope-creep risk**: switching the launcher monorepo to point its
  `.gitmodules` at the new remote submodules, adding CI, or publishing npm
  packages are **out of scope**; record any such opportunity as a separate
  child/discovered work item rather than expanding this task.
- Assumption: the agent creates the repos and pushes (this item is the
  authorisation the F4 producer gate deferred).

## Related work

- **F1** *Design architecture & extraction script with history*
  (CG-0MTRO6P18003AZIZ) — the extraction script and repo-layout contract.
- **F2** *Create core-engine repository* (CG-0MTRO6SZH006EBVN) — core tree.
- **F4** *Per-game repos as single-game launchers (local scaffold)*
  (CG-0MTRO72W5003ECAK) — parent split; producer gate deferred remotes.
- **F5** *Launcher distribution with configs/ presets*
  (CG-0MTRO77XA006YZZC) — the `solo`/`full` presets used for AC4.
- **F7** *Integration verification — full build & test suite*
  (CG-0MTRO7ECL006ID7J) — local sibling verification precedent.
- **F9** *Per-game repos use src/ source root with alias-based core imports*
  (CG-0MUH0NTRG007GDME) — the final layout this task must publish.
- **Epic** *REFACTOR: break out core engine and individual games into their own
  projects* (CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17).
- Reference: `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`,
  `docs/dev/per-game-src-layout-decision.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MRPH9YF0008QIZY** – Document TCE game-development best practices as an agent skill (completed)
- **CG-0MOIXHOWP003Y6E0** – Add runtime audio synthesis for dynamic SFX (WebAudio/Tone.js) (completed)
- **CG-0MM03ITUF1SKCSOZ** – Fix Golf browser test failures in CI (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, access, added, architecture, avoid (+116 more)
- `AGENTS.md` – matched: acceptance, access, added, architecture, avoid (+102 more)
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — matched: 0muh0ntrg007gdme, architecture, beleaguered, blackjack, build (+96 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (visibility) — ANSWERED.** Should the nine new GitHub repositories be
  **public** or **private**? **Answer (producer):** **public**. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-09-26. Adopt `gh repo create --public` for all nine.
- **Q2 (branch model) — ANSWERED.** Which branch should be the **default** and
  what should be pushed? **Answer (producer):** keep the TCE `dev` → `main`
  flow — seed `main` once from the extracted `dev` history (initial
  publication), then continue dev→main promotion via the ship skill. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-09-26. Options considered: (a) `dev` as default;
  (b) seed `main` once then dev→main; (c) single `main`. Answer = (b).
- **Q3 (source revision) — ANSWERED (condition satisfied).** Extract from the
  current `dev` HEAD (record the SHA), or pin to a stable/tagged commit?
  **Answer (producer):** current `dev` HEAD as recommended, **conditional on
  history being maintained** — the producer asked “will this maintain history?
  Can we maintain history?”.
  - **Research (history preservation):** **Yes.** `git filter-repo` retains
    every commit that touched each repo's selected paths, including author,
    date, message and ancestry, so per-file `git log`/`git blame` continuity is
    preserved; the Option C `example-games/<game>/ → src/` rename is applied in
    the same filter pass, so history follows the file to its new path, and the
    result is pushed verbatim (nothing squashed). Evidence:
    `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §“History preservation”;
    `scripts/extract-repos.sh` (`--path-rename` + `--path` filters); F1’s
    recorded retention counts; local probe `git log -- example-games/golf` =
    103 commits, `git log -- example-games/main-street` = 668 commits; the
    GolfScene.ts `--follow` chain reaches its first commit.
  - **Caveat 1 (SHAs change):** because each repo is a filtered *subset*, the
    retained commits are rewritten and receive **new SHAs** — history content
    and provenance are preserved, hash identity with the monorepo is not.
    (This is inherent to any subset split, including `git subtree`.)
  - **Caveat 2 (what we publish):** the extraction clone inherits the
    monorepo's ~150 branches and 17 `v0.1.x` tags; publish only the intended
    refs (see Q4).
  - **Conclusion:** the condition holds — proceed with current `dev` HEAD and
    record `git rev-parse dev` as evidence. Source: interactive reply,
    2026-09-26.
- **Q4 (published refs) — DECISION RECORDED (producer informed via session
  summary; not re-blocked).** Which refs are pushed to the nine new remotes?
  **Recommended and adopted:** push only the intended long-lived branches —
  `dev` plus `main` seeded from it — and do **not** publish the monorepo's
  feature/`wl-*` branches or its `v0.1.x` release tags (those are engine-wide
  and would be misleading on per-game repos). Tag the new repos from their own
  first release. Rationale: matches the `dev`→`main` model in Q2 and avoids
  150+ stale branches / cross-repo tag confusion. Source: agent recommendation
  recorded 2026-09-26; producer may override.

*(Resolved 2026-09-26. This Appendix is updated idempotently; new open items
would be marked OPEN QUESTION.)*

## Plan (2026-09-26)

**Plan: changelog** — 2026-09-26, agent `plan`, session
`herdr-1790434710-2326366-1278`: decomposed this item into six child tasks
(test-first contract → implementation → extraction/scaffold → publication →
fresh-clone verification → docs/evidence/full-suite gate) and wired dependency
edges. No changes were made to this parent's goal or ACs — only this plan block
and the idempotent Appendix revision note below were appended.

### Delivery graph

```
C1 publication decision + test contract          (CG-0MUIND2NE009GPHJ)
     |
     v
C2 publication helper implementation    C3 extract + scaffold + evidence
   (CG-0MUIND4FD000OQB5)                     (CG-0MUIND76O005LRYO)
     |                                        |
     +-------------------+--------------------+
                         v
C4 create the nine public remotes and push dev + seeded main (CG-0MUIND9RO001WKNO)
                         |

                         |

C6 published-state docs, evidence record, full-suite gate (CG-0MUINDGQ7002XVC0)
```

### Children

- **C1** *Decide repo publication mechanism and test contract*
  (CG-0MUIND2NE009GPHJ) — fixes the create/push contract (script vs documented
  commands, `gh repo create --public`, the ref set, idempotency, safety guards)
  and lands the contract tests. **Test-first** item for C2.
- **C2** *Implement the repo publication helper* (CG-0MUIND4FD000OQB5) — makes
  the contract tests pass, adds the `publish:repos` npm script and the tooling
  documentation.
- **C3** *Extract and scaffold the nine repos locally with commit-count
  evidence* (CG-0MUIND76O005LRYO) — runs extraction/scaffold, verifies core +
  golf + main-street locally, captures retained commit counts and source SHA.
- **C4** *Create the nine public GitHub repositories and push dev plus seeded
  main* (CG-0MUIND9RO001WKNO) — the authorised publication (the action the F4
  producer gate deferred).
- **C5** *Verify fresh remote clones: game repos and launcher presets*
  (CG-0MUINDD9Q00725QT) — parent AC3/AC4 verification against fresh remotes.
- **C6** *Publish documented state, record evidence and pass the full-suite
  gate* (CG-0MUINDGQ7002XVC0) — parent AC5/AC7/AC8/AC9.

### Parent AC → child coverage

| Parent AC | Covered by |
|---|---|
| AC1 nine repos exist at the recorded remotes | C4 |
| AC2 final F9 `src/` layout, core holds no games, `core` submodule wiring | C3, C4 |

The automated `run_coverage_review` helper reports `recommendation: proceed`
(it infers 0 parent ACs because the helper reads `- ` bullets while this item's
ACs are numbered `1.`–`9.`); the table above is the authoritative manual mapping
and shows every parent AC is covered.

### Decisions and assumptions recorded in this session (no new producer questions)

1. **Publication mechanism is deliberately left to C1** — the brief allows "an
   end-to-end create+push helper *or* documented commands". C1 decides and
   records it; this plan commits only to a re-runnable, idempotent path with a

# Task: Extract and scaffold the nine repos locally with commit-count evidence

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer I have nine local repos in the final F9 `src/`
layout, each verified to type-check and build, plus the per-repo retained commit
counts and the source `dev` SHA needed as publication evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `git filter-repo` is available (install via the remediation documented in
   `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` when absent); `scripts/extract-repos.sh`
   is executed for all nine targets from the current `dev` HEAD.
2. Extraction runs on clones only: the source monorepo's `git status` is clean
   and its `dev` SHA is unchanged after the run.
3. `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all --core-root <core checkout>
   --repos-dir <parent dir>` scaffolds all eight game repos (writes
   `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `main.ts`, `index.html`
   and `configs/game.json`) and each game repo records the engine as the `core`
   submodule pointing at
   `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`.
4. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` succeed for the extracted core repo,
   `tce-golf` and `tce-main-street`; `npm test -- --project unit` succeeds for
   `tce-golf` and `tce-main-street` against the extracted core checkout.
5. The retained commit count per repo (`git rev-list --count HEAD`) for all nine
   repos and the source `git rev-parse dev` SHA are captured for the parent's
   AC5 evidence.
6. `npx vitest run --project unit tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts
   tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` passes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Install `git filter-repo` and run `scripts/extract-repos.sh` with an
  `--out-dir` outside the monorepo (no writes into the checkout).
- Record the source `dev` SHA **before** extraction and the per-repo commit
  counts immediately after, so the numbers are tied to a known revision.
- Scaffold with `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all` and run the local
  type-check/build/unit gates for core, golf and main-street.
- Change no scripts unless a defect blocks the run; any required script fix is
  recorded as discovered work rather than folded in silently.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/extract-repos.sh` — the extraction driver under test.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — the per-game scaffold driver.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — the partition contract.
- `tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts` — layout/extraction unit suite.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — scaffold unit suite.

**Dependencies:**

None. The F9 `src/` layout is already final and merged on `dev`, so extraction
may proceed in parallel with C1/C2.

**Deliverables:**

- Nine extracted (eight scaffolded) local repos.
- Local build/unit verification evidence for core, golf and main-street.
- Per-repo commit counts and source `dev` SHA.
